title.en: The iron nail in blue solution

text.en: Drop a clean iron nail into blue copper sulphate solution. After a few minutes the nail turns reddish brown and the blue colour fades. Atoms have changed partners, and the way they rearrange decides the type of reaction.

Based on how the atoms of the reactants are rearranged, chemical reactions are classified as combination, decomposition, single displacement and double displacement reactions.
In a combination reaction two or more reactants combine to form one compound, A + B gives AB; it is also called a synthesis reaction.
It can be element plus element, as in 2Na + Cl2 giving 2NaCl, compound plus element, as in PCl3 + Cl2 giving PCl5, or compound plus compound, as in SiO2 + CaO giving CaSiO3.
Most combination reactions are exothermic because forming new bonds releases energy as heat.
In a decomposition reaction a single compound splits into two or more simpler substances; it is the opposite of combination, AB gives A + B.
Decomposition needs energy to break bonds, so it is endothermic; it is called thermal if heat is used, as in 2HgO giving 2Hg + O2, or CaCO3 giving CaO + CO2.
In electrolytic decomposition an electric current is used, as when molten or aqueous sodium chloride gives sodium and chlorine; in photo decomposition light is used, as when silver bromide gives silver and bromine.
In a single displacement reaction a more active element displaces a less active one from its compound, A + BC gives AC + B, as in Zn + 2HCl giving ZnCl2 + H2.
Whether it happens depends on the activity series: iron displaces copper from copper sulphate, Fe + CuSO4 giving FeSO4 + Cu, but silver cannot displace hydrogen from hydrochloric acid.
In a double displacement reaction two compounds exchange ions, AB + CD gives AD + CB; it is also called metathesis.
If an insoluble solid forms, such as yellow lead iodide when potassium iodide meets lead nitrate, it is a precipitation reaction; an acid reacting with a base to give salt and water is a neutralization reaction.
To tell the types apart, count the reactants and products: one product means combination, one reactant means decomposition, an element plus a compound means single displacement, and two compounds swapping ions means double displacement.

problem.en: Classify each reaction: (a) CaCO3 gives CaO + CO2 on heating, (b) Fe + CuSO4 gives FeSO4 + Cu, (c) 2H2 + O2 gives 2H2O.

text.en: (a) One compound splits into two simpler substances using heat, so it is a thermal decomposition reaction.

why.en: Single reactant, more than one product.

text.en: (b) Iron, an element, replaces copper in the compound, so it is a single displacement reaction; iron is above copper in the activity series.

why.en: Element plus compound gives compound plus element.

text.en: (c) Two elements join to make one compound, so it is a combination reaction, and it is exothermic.

prompt.en: Name the four types of reactions, give one equation for each, and tell how you identify them.

requiredIdeas.en: Combination, decomposition, single and double displacement
Number and kind of reactants and products

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking every reaction between a metal and an acid is double displacement
Ignoring the activity series when predicting displacement

points.en: Combination: A + B gives AB; decomposition: AB gives A + B (thermal, electrolytic, photo).
Single displacement: a more active element displaces a less active one; use the activity series.
Double displacement: exchange of ions, giving a precipitate or salt and water.
Combination is usually exothermic and decomposition is endothermic.
